subject: TTFT streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@scaleflow.ai>, Lane Carter <lane@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: TTFT streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps

Hi Samir / Lane —

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation. Quick recap of the performance targets and open questions so we can align the bench plan and next steps: 

Recap (from your notes):
- Target time-to-first-token (TTFT): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms (you mentioned p95 could be relaxed up to ~300ms)
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200–250 requests/sec at peak
- Expected concurrency: ~50–60 concurrent user sessions
- Streaming behavior: client expects streaming responses for long outputs (SSE or WebSocket). Preferred chunk cadence: ~200ms, tolerable up to 300ms. Chunk sizes ~1–4 tokens per chunk typical for your app.
- Model family: medium-sized open model (we discussed 7B / 13B class) — please confirm exact model you plan to evaluate.

Open items / asks for the bench run:
1) Please confirm the canonical model and a representative sample payload (one short prompt and one long streaming prompt).
2) Confirm whether WebSocket is required or if SSE is acceptable for your infra.
3) Any PII/data handling constraints for the test payloads? (we can scrub or run inside a private deployment if needed)
4) Requested SLOs to validate: TTFT p50/p95, sustained throughput (rps), and streaming chunk cadence/latency.

Next steps we propose:
- Rishi to run an initial TTFT + streaming cadence benchmark on a Dedicated instance using your sample payloads (should be a 2–4 hour run).
- We’ll share a short SLO draft for sign-off (attached: marissa-ttft-recap.pdf).
- Schedule a 30-min results review call after the bench run — suggested window: next Wed or Thu.

Attachments: marissa-ttft-recap.pdf (recap + initial SLO template)

If that all looks right, Samir — can you send the sample payloads and confirm WebSocket vs SSE preference?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
redwoodinference.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-24T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TTFT streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick notes from the SE side (plan + technical constraints):

Plan:
- I’ll run a focused TTFT benchmark and streaming cadence verification on a Dedicated node configured with a model equivalent to 13B FP16/INT8 if you confirm model family. The run will capture p50/p95 TTFT, sustained rps at target concurrency, and per-chunk latency distribution for streaming.
- Testbed: 1 dedicated GPU pool, synthetic load matching 200/250 rps and an escalating concurrency sweep (10/25/50/60).
- Streaming modes: we’ll run with both SSE and WebSocket endpoints to compare chunk latency and server push behavior. WebSocket may add ~5–10ms overhead but is often more resilient for bi-directional flows.

Suggested SLO thresholds to validate (engineering POV):
- TTFT p50: < 100ms ideally (we can often hit ~70–90ms for 13B with optimizations)
- TTFT p95: < 250ms target (300ms tolerable, but we should root-cause tail spikes)
- Sustained throughput: validate linearity up to 250 rps; watch GPU utilization and KV cache hit rates
- Streaming chunk cadence: aim for <= 200ms between chunks at p50/p75; p95 <= 300ms

Data/inputs needed from customer:
- Representative prompt set (short + long streaming prompts) — for streaming long outputs include expected average output length (tokens) and typical prefix lengths.
- Confirmation on WebSocket vs SSE preference.
- Any samples of client-side chunk-aggregation behavior (if the client batches incoming chunks before rendering).

I’ll prepare a short bench plan doc (ttft-benchmark-plan.md) and start the run as soon as we have payloads. I’ll include raw logs and a short summary CSV for TTFT and chunk cadence.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: TTFT streaming SLOs — follow-up & next steps

Samir / Lane —

Following up on Rishi’s plan. We can run both SSE and WebSocket tests, but please confirm which one is your preferred production path (helps prioritize tuning).

Proposed calendar:
- Please send sample payloads by end of day Monday (I attached a short SLO draft for review: SLO-draft.pdf).
- Rishi to run the bench on Tuesday/Wednesday.
- Results review call: Wed 3/31 or Thu 4/1 — I’ll send a calendar invite once we have a preferred slot.

Also: small ask on payloads — include one long prompt that triggers streaming (expected output >= 300 tokens) and an expected client-side rendering cadence. That helps us match chunk cadence to your UX.

Marissa / Rishi —

Thanks — confirmed on our side. A few clarifications and the sample payloads attached.

Confirmed targets (we’re okay to validate these in the bench run):
- TTFT: p50 <= 150ms, p95 <= 300ms (we can discuss tighter p50 later)
- Peak throughput: 250 rps
- Concurrency: 60 simultaneous sessions
- Streaming: prefer WebSocket in production, but SSE is acceptable for the bench. Aim for ~200ms chunk cadence.

Attached: sample-payloads.json (short_prompt, long_streaming_prompt). No sensitive PII; these are sanitized.

We’re available for the results review on Wed 3/31 morning PT. Please go ahead and schedule.

—Samir
